name: CursorBench
intro: CursorBench 是 Cursor 基于内部工程团队真实会话持续更新的编程智能体评测套件，使用模糊、多文件、多工具和多步骤任务衡量真实开发效用。
build_method: 用 Cursor Blame 将已提交代码追溯到生成它的智能体请求，形成开发者请求与标准解法对，并从内部/受控来源筛选、每隔数月刷新
metric: 公开排行榜：正确性得分、单任务平均成本、Token 数、步骤数；内部另评代码质量、效率和交互行为
eval_feature: 智能体裁判接受多种有效解法；离线评测与受控线上实验交叉验证
build_method_en: Use Cursor Blame to trace committed code to the agent request that produced it, pair the developer query with its ground-truth solution, curate internal/controlled sources, and refresh every few months
eval_feature_en: Agentic graders accept multiple valid solutions; offline results are cross-checked with controlled online experiments
intro_en: CursorBench is Cursor's continuously updated internal coding-agent suite, built from real engineering sessions and ambiguous, multi-file, multi-tool, multi-step development tasks.
metric_en: Public leaderboard: correctness score, average cost per task, tokens, and steps; internal axes also include code quality, efficiency, and interaction behavior
drawio_review_note: Aligned with Cursor's official March 2026 methodology post and live CursorBench 3.1 leaderboard, not inferred from third-party model system cards. Cursor Blame traces committed code back to the agent request that produced it, yielding a natural developer-query/ground-truth-solution pair. Tasks come mainly from Cursor's internal codebase and controlled sources, are refreshed every few months, and intentionally use short, ambiguous descriptions. Version 3.0 focused on edit, refactor, and bug-fix tasks; 3.1 adds codebase understanding, bug finding, planning, and code review, and revises some edit-task grading criteria. Agents run against an initialized codebase and are graded by agentic graders that can accept multiple valid solutions. Cursor discloses correctness, code quality, efficiency, and interaction behavior as internal axes, while the public 3.1 leaderboard reports Score, average cost per task, tokens, and steps; cost applies each model's published input/cache-read/cache-write/output token prices. Controlled online experiments validate whether offline rankings track developer outcomes. Because the task distribution changes, scores must be compared only within the same eval version. Task instances, suite size, grader prompts/rubrics, harness, and per-item outputs remain proprietary and are explicitly marked as undisclosed.
